verdict.rationale: Pydantic AI documents running agents in the terminal: the `clai` CLI, launching CLI mode from any Agent via `Agent.to_cli_sync()`, and calling agents as plain objects with run(). TestModel/FunctionModel also support model-free test runs. However, the documented CLI is framed as interactive chat. There is no evidence of non-interactive, scriptable execution of the framework's shipped example agents for automated verification. missing for 10: documented runnable example agents, a headless/non-interactive CLI mode (e.g. single prompt with machine-readable output and exit codes), independent hands-on corroboration of agent-driven verification.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can run the framework's example agents headlessly from a terminal so an agent can verify what it just built

citations.quote: you can directly launch CLI mode from an `Agent` instance using `Agent.to_cli_sync()`
The same agent runs everywhere you need it: behind a web frontend, in the terminal, on a voice call, on a durable background queue, or as a plain object you call run() on.
Pydantic AI comes with a CLI, clai (pronounced “clay”). You can use it to chat with various LLMs and quickly get answers, right from the command line
Pydantic AI also comes with TestModel and FunctionModel for testing and development.
